title: Design System: Syntix Official Results Bulletin

display-mark.purpose: Oversized editorial numerals or initials used as quiet section artwork.

headline.purpose: Page titles and primary workflow headings.

micro-label.purpose: Dense overlines and diagram annotations at 10px.

operational-number.purpose: Scores, rankings, totals, and high-scan values.

shadows.name: temporary-layer
shadows.purpose: Structural separation for dialogs and drawers only.

motion.name: state-change
motion.purpose: Short color and border transitions on controls.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single clearest next action in an operational region.

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: A reversible or supporting action beside the primary choice.

components.name: Danger Button
components.description: A destructive or irreversible action that requires deliberate contrast.

components.name: Text Field
components.description: A compact field with an explicit label and visible focus state.

components.name: Status Tag
components.description: A compact textual state marker that never relies on color alone.

components.name: Ruled Bulletin Section
components.description: The standard flat container for one administrative topic.

narrative.overview:
Syntix is the official event record in motion. Its interface borrows the authority and legibility of a posted results bulletin: bright paper, dark ink, crisp rules, compact operational labels, and a restrained cyan action color. It should feel trustworthy under event-day pressure, not decorative or theatrical.

The system is information-dense without becoming cramped. Hierarchy comes from typography, alignment, rules, and quiet tonal changes rather than stacks of floating cards. Global Admin and organizer screens use the same visual language as Judge and Tabulator work, while preserving each workflow's established structure.
keyCharacteristics: Ink-navy hierarchy with cyan actions and restrained gold signals
Flat surfaces separated by hairline rules
Compact labels and condensed operational numerals
Clear next actions and explicit record states

rules.name: The Cyan Is Action Rule
rules.body: Action Cyan identifies interaction, progress, or focus. Do not use it as broad decoration.

rules.name: The Gold Is Rare Rule
rules.body: Bulletin Gold marks exceptional event context. It must not compete with primary actions.

rules.name: The Numbers Carry State Rule
rules.body: Use condensed numerals for important operational values, not for paragraphs or ordinary control labels.

rules.name: The Ruled Paper Rule
rules.body: Prefer a hairline border or quiet surface shift before introducing a shadow.

dos: Do use Ink Navy and typographic weight to establish authority before adding color.
Do separate dense content with Hairline Rule borders and Quiet Paper bands.
Do keep score, approval, and result states explicit in text.
Do preserve 44px touch targets and visible keyboard focus.
Do use Barlow Condensed for scores, totals, rankings, and other compact operational numbers.
donts: Don't add dark mode or dark event-control styling. Syntix is permanently light.
Don't build generic white-and-blue SaaS screens from rounded cards and soft shadows.
Don't use cyan or gold as broad decoration.
Don't hide official status behind color, icons, or hover-only content.
Don't change an established admin workflow merely to make it resemble the Judge scorecard.
